issues.legal_issue: An eviction application under the rent-control order cannot be maintained against a partnership firm solely in the firm name when the partners are not joined individually.
material_facts: A landlord brought an eviction application under the rent-control order against a partnership in its firm name, seeking eviction for personal occupation and essential repairs.
The partners were not individually joined as respondents.
The Code of Civil Procedure did not apply to proceedings under the rent-control order.
issues.conclusion: The application could not be maintained against the partnership in its firm name alone because the procedure allowing a firm to sue or be sued in that name did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Order 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a firm to sue and be sued in its own name without joining the partners, but that Code does not apply to proceedings under the Central Provinces and Berar Letting of Houses and Rent Control Order, 1949. Accordingly, an eviction application under clauses 13(3)(vi) and (vii) of that Order cannot be maintained against a firm in its firm name alone. No earlier cases are relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and partnership_named_as_respondent and partners_not_individually_joined and ordinary_firm_naming_procedure_unavailable

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction under a rent-control regime.
predicates.partnership_named_as_respondent: The applicant names a partnership as the respondent by its firm name.
predicates.partners_not_individually_joined: The applicant does not join the partners individually as respondents.
predicates.ordinary_firm_naming_procedure_unavailab: The procedural rule that ordinarily allows a firm to sue or be sued in its own name does not apply to the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding under rent control names a partnership by its firm name, omits its individual partners, and cannot use the ordinary firm-naming procedure, an application against the firm name alone is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Omitting the individual partners from an eviction application against a partnership is a correctable misdescription rather than a defect requiring dismissal when the partners are before the court under the firm name.
material_facts: The eviction application named the partnership firm but did not individually name its partners.
The firm was a compendious name for the partners, who were before the court under that name.
The landlord sought to amend the application to add the partners as respondents and make consequential amendments.
issues.conclusion: The omission was a misdescription that could be corrected at any stage, not a ground to dismiss the application. The Court allowed the amendment and remitted the matter to the Rent Controller for disposal on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: A partnership firm is a compendious name for the partners constituting it. Although the firm could not be sued in its firm name alone in a proceeding to which the Code of Civil Procedure did not apply, naming the firm instead of its partners was a misdescription that could be corrected at any stage. No earlier cases are relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and partnership_named_as_respondent and partners_not_individually_joined and partners_identifiable_as_constituents

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction under a rent-control regime.
predicates.partnership_named_as_respondent: The applicant names a partnership as the respondent by its firm name.
predicates.partners_not_individually_joined: The applicant does not join the partners individually as respondents.
predicates.partners_identifiable_as_constituents: The persons constituting the partnership are identifiable and are before the court under the firm name.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction proceeding names a partnership by its firm name without individually joining identifiable partners who are before the court under that name, the respondent misdescription can be corrected.
